Commentary.Commentary: Talking about this innings, Sri Lanka after gaining a big first innings' lead started positively. Dimuth Karunaratne once again batted superbly to notch up a score beyond fifty. The middle lower order though disappointed again, some vital runs from the tail pushed the target towards 350. South Africa's bowling was neither too bad in the first innings nor in the second. Kagiso Rabada managed to pick three while Keshav Maharaj also found his rhythm to bag a 4-fer. Over to their batsmen now who have a big job to save/win this Test. Let's see what happens on the other side as there is still some time to go before Lunch.

Right then, Sri Lanka added 79 runs to their overnight total and have taken their lead past the 350-run mark. South Africa bowled well this morning to pick six wickets but their real challenge begins now. The pitch is offering assistance for the spinners but they can take solace from Lakmal's batting. In spite of not being a very technically sound batsman, he showed with his stroke play that there ain't any demons in the pitch and if applied well, it's possible to survive.

OUT! A soft dismissal. Steyn bangs it in short outside off, Sandakan is on his toes as he flays at it. Middles his shot properly but it doesn't have enough elevation to go over the point fielder. Bavuma there makes no mistake and Sri Lanka are all out for 190, setting a daunting target of 352 for the Proteas. Also, this is Steyn's 421st wicket and he equals Shaun Pollock as the all-time highest wicket-taker for South Africa in Tests.

FOUR! The lead goes past 350! Back of a length delivery outside off, Sandakan gets back to punch it through the line. Doesn't quite middle it as it travels off the outer half of the bat but right through the gap between gully and point for a boundary.
A wayward bouncer, wide outside off, Sandakan allows it through to the keeper.
A good length ball outside off, punched off the back foot to point.
Dale Steyn returns into the attack.

Tossed up ball on middle, turning in, Sandakan being a chinaman bowler himself, reads it quite well and works it in front of square leg for a single. The partnership is worth 23 runs and it has come in a quick time also. The lead is 3 short of 350!
Spinning down the leg side, Lakmal fails to flick and it goes off his pads towards short fine leg. He looks at his partner who is ready to change strike. They take a leg bye.
Too full and on off, Lakmal digs it out safely.
Lands this one around leg, turning down, Lakmal tries to flick but misses.
Full and flighted outside off, driven to mid off.
FOUR! Lakmal is showing that there is nothing wrong with the pitch. Takes a long stride forward to a full ball outside off and drives it delightfully through extra cover for a boundary.
A low full toss on off, it's been driven down to long off for a single. Retains strike.
Flighted full on off, defended off the front foot by Lakmal.
FOUR! Flatter and shorter outside off, Lakmal goes deep inside the crease and plays a cracking square cut. Beats the point fielder for a boundary.
Loopy and on off, defended off the front foot.
Too full and on middle, worked wide of mid on for a single.
Shortish and on off, punched wide of mid off for a run.
Slips one down the leg side, Sandakan fails to get it away off his pads.
Driven through mid off by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Tries to drive this one but gets an inside edge onto the pads. It loops in the air and drops on the off side. Then it turns towards the leg side. Plenty of revolutions on the ball.
Full and on middle, spinning back in, Lakmal tries to swing it over the mid-wicket region but misses. He is hit on the pads but it's missing leg.

FOUR! Good shot! The skipper continues to add handy runs. Shamsi throws it up wide outside off, Lakmal latches onto it and smacks it past his partner at the other end. The mid off is up and a boundary results.
Turning down the leg side, Lakmal tries to flick but misses.
Tossed up ball on off, defended off the front foot.
Suranga has punched that ball through the off side. They pick up a single.
Lakmal has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
FOUR! Flighted and full on middle, turning in, Lakmal clears his front leg and smashes it over mid on for a boundary.
Goes back and cuts but finds the point fielder.
Gets on the front foot and defends.
Driven through mid off by the batsman.

Lakshan Sandakan is the last batsman. The umpire had called it over but proactiveness from the third umpire saves everyone from the embarrassment. One more to go, sorry guys, says umpire Tucker as he returns to his mark.

OUT! Gone! Shamsi finally gets lucky with his appealing. Traps Herath in front. A flighted full ball landing around leg and spinning towards off, Herath goes down on one knee to sweep but misses and is rapped on the back leg. They appeal and the finger goes up this time. Rangana opts for the referral but it turns out to be of no help. The replays confirmed the pitching of the ball to be within the line and it has hit Herath in line as well. The ball is heading for the stumps afterwards and hence the onfield call stays.
Review time again. This time from the batsman. Rangana Herath it is. Looks dead in front to us.

Another appeal for an lbw but this one short lived as Shamsi immediately pulls out. Turning back into the batsman from outside off, some extra bounce too, Herath fails to defend and is hit high on the pads. Impact also looked outside off.

Not out! No inside edge but it's turning back in too much and will miss the stumps. Floated ball on off, landing full and spinning back in. Lakmal tries to defend off his front foot but misses and hits him on the pads. They put in an unsuccessful appeal and South Africa take the DRS. Nothing doing in the replays and Lakmal survives.
Shout for an lbw! It's not given by the umpire and Tabraiz Shamsi convinces his skipper to take the referral. Inside edge?
FOUR! Very full and on off, spinning back in, Lakmal drills it straight back down the ground for a cracking boundary. Vital runs, taking Sri Lanka's lead towards 350.
Shout for an lbw! Not given. Floated full ball around leg, spinning down, Lakmal tries to defend but misses and is hit on the pads. Missing leg.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Tossed up ball outside off, Herath tries to be innovative. Attempts a reverse sweep but misses. The keeper also misses the ball and they take a couple of leg byes.
Loopy and full on off, Herath is forward in defense.
Rangana Herath is the number 10 batsman.

OUT! Bowled 'em! Maharaj gets a four-fer! He tosses this one up in the air and lands it full around middle. It straightens a bit after hitting the deck as Mathews sits down on one knee to play the slog sweep. Misses the ball completely and it goes on to disturb the wooden framework. The last recognized batsman departs with Sri Lanka leading by 317 runs.
Flighted and full outside off, Mathews drives it back to the bowler. From the inside half of the willow.
Fullish around leg, Mathews presents a straight bat in defense.
Tossed up ball wide outside off, Lakmal drives it through the line but finds the extra cover fielder.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Flights this one and bowls it around off, Lakmal throws his bat at it and smashes it to deep cover. They take only a couple. Poor running from Mathews. He thought it's going to the boundary but the ball slowed down. Also, he was running with the gloves in the hands. Poor.
Lakmal has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Loopy and on middle, spinning in, Lakmal clears his front leg and goes hard at it. The ball takes the inner half of his bat and rolls to mid on.
Very full on off, pushed back towards mid off.
Turning away from the batsman, Mathews tries to defend but it takes the outer half of the bat and rolls to short third man.
SIX! Fine, fine shot! Opens up the stumps by moving to the leg side and then lofts it with the spin over covers. Lovely connection and it has gone all the way for a maximum. Top shot, Angelo.
Fullish and on off, pushed back towards the bowler.

Too full and on leg, it's flicked wide of mid on and they cross for a quick single. Amla scores a direct hit at the bowler's end but no harm done. It ricochets, they think of the second but Bavuma is quick to the ball and they stop in their tracks.
Loopy on off, Lakmal this time goes the aerial route. Not quite from the middle of the bat but it loops over the bowler's head and they take a couple of runs.
Flighted full ball on off, Lakmal defends it back to the bowler.
Spin from both ends now. Keshav Maharaj to roll his arm.

Big turn and bounce into the batsman from around off, Lakmal gets back to work it around but misses and is hit high on the pads. Only a muted appeal follows. The ball in the meanwhile rolls to point and they cross for a leg bye.
Flighted and too full outside off, Lakmal tries to hit it but misses. It gets deflected off de Kock's gloves to short leg.
Very full and outside off, a mistimed off drive down to long off for a single.
Floated ball, landing outside off and turning back in, Mathews gets deep inside the crease and defends it out safely in spite of the ball staying low.
Flighted full ball on off, flicked on the leg side but short leg did well to stick his left hand out in order to stop the ball.
A low full toss on off, pushed back to the bowler.
Tabraiz Shamsi into the attack.

Drinks break. South Africa have done well to pick three wickets but the worrying factor for them is that the lead has already crossed the 300-run mark. They would like to polish the tail quickly unlike the first innings which in a way has hurt them big time in this Test match. Just imagine, the Lankan lead would have been close to just 50, had the last two wickets not added 111 runs. Expect spinners to operate in the next hour.
This one cuts back into the batsman from a length outside off, Lakmal fails to defend and gets hit high on the pads. A stifled appeal immediately dies down.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
A length ball outside off, punched to covers for a single.
Good length ball on middle, defended on the leg side.
Short and on middle, pulled to long leg for one.
Width on offer outside off, Lakmal drives but finds the cover fielder.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.

Aerial and the short cover fielder nearly came into the picture. Rabada bangs in a short ball on middle, Lakmal tries to fend at it but the bat turns in his hands and he gets it away off the leading edge. It pops out but lands wide of the close-in fielder.
A short cover in place, right in the face of Lakmal.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Good length delivery outside off, holding its line, Mathews pushes at it and edges it behind. Du Plessis at second slip dives to his right and makes a good stop as it comes to him on the bounce.
Mathews has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
On a length around off, defended off the back foot.
Full and around off, this one is bowled in the 140s, Lakmal is all over the place with his footwork as he defends it somehow on the leg side.
Huge cry for an lbw! The umpire turns it down. Steyn spears in a full ball on middle and leg, angling further down, Lakmal is beaten for pace as he tries to flick. Missing leg.
On a length and outside off, Lakmal flashes and misses.
Shortish and pulled wide of mid-wicket for a couple of runs. Lead crosses 300!
Taps it down to covers and collects a single.
Short and wide outside off, cut through point for a couple of runs.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Sliding down the leg side, Lakmal gets into a tangle as he decides to leave it. Takes a blow on his thigh pad.
Skipper Suranga Lakmal is in next.

OUT! Rabada strikes again. Perera had a bat in his hands but forgot to use it. Kagiso gets some appreciable movement going on this delivery. It lands on a length outside off and nips back in. Perera misreads it and offers no shot after taking his front leg a little forward. It raps him on the back leg, the bend knee, they appeal and the finger goes up. Impact cannot be an issue and the umpire is sure that it has come back in enough to hit the stumps. Dilruwan did have a chat regarding the use of the DRS but Mathews advised him not to. A good decision as the replays confirm that it's hitting the top of off pole. With this wicket, Rabada becomes the third quickest South African bowler to pick 150 wickets, behind Tayfield and Steyn. Also, he is the youngest ever to achieve this feat. He is special.
This one is angled in on middle, Perera clips it through backward square leg and takes a couple of runs.
Dilruwan Perera is the new batsman.

OUT! The 'round the wicket angle has worked for Rabada. He angles in a length ball from outside off, no movement from the pitch this time as it follows the direction of the bowler's arm. Dickwella with an unsure footwork plays at it and nicks it behind to de Kock. He makes no mistake and South Africa taste second success this morning.
Fine shot! A fuller length ball outside off, Niroshan drives it square of the wicket on the off side. The point fielder chases it and they take a couple of runs.

Runs in from 'round the wicket and lands it on a shortish length outside off. Dickwella punches it with ease through covers. Shamsi chases it down in the deep as the ball slows down and the batsmen collect three runs.
On a length around off, Dickwella punches it off his back foot to covers.

Angles in a length ball around off, staying low, Mathews keeps his eyes on the ball and then tries to defend. But it catches the toe end of the bat and rolls past the diving gully fielder who gets some hand on it. A single taken.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Mathews has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Nearly a yorker, if not a yorker exactly. It's outside off, Dickwella tries to dig it out but is beaten for pace.
Punches a length ball to covers where Maharaj quickly reacts to his right and stops the ball.

FOUR! Poor delivery and punished. Rabada continues to drop it short but this time the line is taking it down the leg side. Dickwella just helps it around with the pull shot and finds the fence at fine leg. The fielder in the deep was a bit square and had no chance of cutting it off.
Sharp delivery, shortish and outside off, Dickwella tries to force it through covers but it takes the inside edge and goes to mid-wicket.
Back of a length delivery angling into the batsman, Dickwella defends it off his back foot.
A short leg comes in now for Dickwella. A long leg in place too. Expect some short stuff as Rabada is running in from 'round the wicket.
A length ball outside off, staying a bit low, Mathews hangs back and and pushes it towards covers for a quick single.
A shot attempted out of sheer frustration. Steyn serves this one up and wide outside off. Niroshan throws his bat at it but fails to connect.
In the line of the stumps, defended off the back foot.

They needed a short leg there. Steyn delivers an effort ball. Bends his back to extract some extra bounce from the middle stump line. Dickwella is caught in an awkward position as he tries to fend at it. It comes off from the shoulder of his bat and lobs in the air. Steyn runs forward but it dies down immediately in front of him. Doubt even short leg would have done anything about it.
A short mid-wicket in.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
A length ball on off, defended off the back foot.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
Presses forward to a length ball and pushes it to covers.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back oot.
Works it in the gap at mid-wicket and picks up a single.
Stays on the back foot and taps it down on the off side.
Shortish and outside off, Mathews punches it from the back foot, a bit uppish but through backward point for a couple of runs.
Niroshan Dickwella is in next with Sri Lanka leading by 278 runs.

OUT! Gone! A very unfortunate way to get dismissed. Rabada serves a full length ball outside off, Mathews mistimes his drive back towards the bowler off the inner half of his bat. Kagiso gets down low to stop the ball but it brushes his fingers and goes on to hit the stumps at the other end. Silva was backing up way too much and quickly turns to park his bat inside the crease. As soon as it hits the timber, the Proteas go up in a big appeal. The third umpire is referred who by mistake first started to look for caught and bowled but then immediately corrected himself. The replays show the clear deflection of the ball from Rabada's hands and then Roshen is found well short of the crease. An accidental run out as Rabada was looking to stop the ball and wasn't trying at all to deflect it behind. A lucky breakthrough for South Africa early in the morning. A fast fact - Roshen Silva averages 130 in the third innings of a Test match and if the tourists know about it, it's a big breakthrough.
Appeal for a run out at the non-striker's end. Kagiso Rabada is all smiles and the South Africans are celebrating. The umpire has referred it upstairs...
This one is bowled in the high-130s. On a length around off, it's been blocked from the back foot by Roshen.
A length ball on off, 140.4 kph, Silva defends it from the crease to mid-wicket.
On a driving length outside off, holding its line, Silva takes a stride forward before shouldering arms.
Once again the line is very straight. Mathews helps this good length delivery through square leg to collect another single in this over.
Steyn tries to repeat the last delivery but from the middle stump line. It turns out to be too straight in line and Roshen works it through square leg for a single.
Play and a miss! Excellent delivery, lands it on a good length outside off and gets it to straighten a bit, Silva pokes at it tentatively and gets beaten.
Bumper, nicely-targeted, Angelo lets it through over his head by crouching a bit.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
With gentle hands Silva pushes this one in the cover region and then steals a quick single.

Some issue with the ball which is quickly addressed by the umpire. Seems some part of the leather has come off and Vernon Philander brings that to the notice. One of the two umpires cut it with the help of a scissor.
Fullish and around off, angling in, Silva gets on the front foot and defends it with soft hands.
Some movement off the seam this time. From a length around off. Mathews works it off the inner portion of the bat to fine leg for one.
Full and around off, defended off the front foot to the on side.
Kagiso Rabada to share the attack from the other end. The field remains the same - two slips and a gully.
Stays back footed and then pushes it towards the cover fielder.
Good length ball on off, Silva punches it off his back foot to covers.
Digs in a short delivery this time, outside off, Mathews pulls it in front of square leg for a run.
Angles in a length ball on off, Mathews once again remains back footed before keeping it out on the leg side.
On a length and just around off, Mathews goes on the back foot and plays it down to mid-wicket.
Begins the day's play with a fuller length ball on off, angling in, Silva flicks it through backward square leg and takes a single.

Time to get underway. The South Africa players are taking the field. Out come the overnight batsmen - Angelo Mathews and Roshen Silva. The latter will be on strike. Dale Steyn to begin proceedings. Some good breeze is blowing across the stadium and the pacers would like to make use of it. Two slips and a gully in place. Here we go...

Rangana Herath says that his fingers are fine now and he has fully recovered. Mentions that Perera and all the spinners did a remarkable job. Feels it's not an easy pitch to bat as it's gripping and the bounce is indifferent. Is hoping to get the same result with the ball in the last innings as he believes that chasing in excess of 250 is never easy on a Galle pitch. On his plans for the future, he says that he needs to have a proper chat with the captain, coach and the management. Informs that he has decided to retire after the England tour and smiles before stating that his time has come and it's time to pass the torch to the youngsters.

Pitch report - Shaun Pollock and Kepler Wessels combine to inspect the playing area. The former started by saying that Russel Arnold yesterday mentioned that this surface has more bounce than turn which he has not seen before. Wessels adds to it by saying that it's a dry surface and from Sri Lanka's point of view it's turning straight from the line of the stumps. Also adds that there is not a lot of rough to work with and feels that it's going to spin more and more. Advice from Wessels - 'You cannot play a survival game here and need to attack as well!'
Weather - There was some overnight rain but the groundsmen did well to protect the playing area. The sun has come out this morning and the ground is ready for a prompt start.

Hello and welcome ladies and gentlemen for the third day of the Galle Test. A tough day awaits South Africa who are staring down the barrel. They will require a monumental effort to make a comeback in this game, whether they manage that or not only time will tell. The hosts will look to maximize the damage by taking their lead close to 350, if not more. The pitch is playing all kind of tricks and batting is only going to get tougher from here on. Expect a riveting day's play.
...DAY 3, FIRST SESSION...

Right then, this match is heavily loaded in favour of the home team. They can call the shots from here. Already they have a good enough lead in the pocket and would like to bat freely to build on it. South Africa will know that they have an uphill task in front but that's when they will come out to chase. First thing first, their aim will be to bundle out the hosts as soon as possible on Saturday. Promises to be yet another cracking day. Do join us at 1000 local (0430 GMT) for all the action. Meanwhile, you can switch over to the Pakistan vs Zimbabwe ODI. Cheers!

Shaun Pollock catches up with Keshav Maharaj for a little chat. The South African spinner looks pleased after finding some rhythm and says that he was just looking to bowl simple line and length. Admits that he was a bit rusty in the first innings. Also adds that it's very enjoyable to play in the subcontinent. On his team's batting performance, Maharaj states that they didn't bat according to the plan but he is still hopeful to force a collapse on the third morning and then chase down the total. Speaking on the nature of the pitch, he believes that if a batsman gets in, it becomes a lot easier as depicted by Dimuth Karunaratne's knock in the first innings. On how will they be celebrating Faf du Plessis' birthday, Maharaj smiles and says that there won't be much celebration tonight as they would look to relax and rest to brace themselves for the challenges of Day 3.

The day entirely belonged to the Sri Lankan spinners. They wreaked havoc in the morning session and completely broke the South African batting. Apart from one stand between Faf du Plessis and Vernon Philander, there wasn't much resistance offered by the Protea batsmen. They appeared pretty clueless and to be honest, lacked the temperament to survive on a demanding pitch against world-class bowlers.

A good session for South Africa in terms of wickets but in the overall scenario, they are way behind the 8-ball, trailing by 272 runs to be precise. On a pitch assisting the spinners, Keshav Maharaj left his impression by picking three wickets while Kagiso Rabada bagged the prized scalp of Dimuth Karunaratne. The Sri Lankan opener once again displayed immense character in his knock and it appeared that he was batting on a completely different track. Such was his command over his innings. He was unfortunate to miss out on the opportunity to equal Tillakaratne Dilshan's record of scoring a twin century in his 50th Test.
Once again a googly by Shamsi, Mathews stays back footed in defense. That will be Stumps on day 2!
A wrong 'un on middle, Mathews gets deep inside the crease, attempting to work it on the leg side without picking the variation. Somehow he keeps it out and then smiles.
Gets forward to defend but it takes the outer portion of the bat and rolls wide of point. A single taken.

Whoa! That missed everything! Beauty by Shamsi. Lets out a loopy full ball around off, fuller in length, Silva gets forward to work it away but it spins back in, beats the inside edge and flies over the stumps to the fence behind. Given as runs. Ohho, nicely spotted by the umpire. The replays confirm the involvement of a thin inside edge.
Flighted and on middle, helped away to fine leg for a single.

Tossed up ball on off, Mathews moves back and works it in front of square leg for a single. Bavuma there slides to stop the ball and then scores a direct hit at the non-striker's end. It deflects behind with no one backing up and they take an overthrow.
Tabraiz Shamsi to bowl the last over of the day.
Very full and on middle, Silva keeps it out to mid-wicket.
Floated and on off, defended off the front foot.

Edged! Did that carry??? No is the answer. Nervy moment for Roshen. A fantastic delivery by Keshav. Serves it full and on middle, spinning away, once again Silva tries to defend off his front foot but it spins away to take a soft outside edge. It hurries behind towards Amla at first slip who goes down low but it appears that the ball dropped in front.
Loopy and on off, it's defended in front of silly point.
Dean Elgar comes in at silly point.
Leans forward to a full ball and defends it to the off side.
Flighted and full on off, defended back off the front foot.

EDGY FOUR! Very loose from Mathews. Throws his bat at a length ball outside off and gets it away off the outside edge. It flies wide of the slip cordon and speeds to the third man fence. 100 up for Sri Lanka with that airy fairy shot.
On a good length around off, shaping back into the batsman, Angelo covers the line and movement before pushing it back to the bowler.
Drops it on a length and just outside off, Mathews remains on the back foot and pushes it with an angled bat to point.
Sharp delivery, full and on middle, Roshen offers a straight bat and pushes it down to mid on. They cross for a brisk single.
Rabada spears this one full and on off, it has been kept out safely by Silva at covers.
Effort delivery. Bends his back and delivers it on a shortish length around off, Roshen drops his wrists and allows it through to the keeper.
Flatter and fuller on middle, drilled down to mid on.
Beauty of a delivery! Drifting into the batsman and landing full on off. Mathews tries to play the line but it spins away to beat the outside edge.
Very full and on middle, Mathews is solidly behind in line as he defends it to the leg side.
Floated and full on off, Mathews lunges and defends it with a loose bottom hand.
A little bit more air this time, full and on middle, it's flicked in front of square leg for a couple.
Tossed up ball on middle, defended off the front foot to the leg side.
The batsman picked that bouncer early and let it through to the keeper.

FOUR! Off the pair in an edgy manner. Rabada pitches it full and around off, Silva gets forward to play at it but it takes the outside edge and screams past the gully fielder for a boundary at third man.
Full and outside off, driven off the front foot to mid off.
Roshen Silva is the new batsman, no nightwatchman employed by Sri Lanka with 27 balls left in the day's play.

OUT! So after 301 balls, South Africa have managed to see the back of Dimuth Karunaratne. Rabada steams in from 'round the wicket and dishes out a back of a length ball outside off. It straightens just a touch after pitching as Karunaratne goes on the back foot to punch it through the line. But it takes a thick outside edge and flies to wide first slip where Amla takes a fine low catch. End of a brilliant, brilliant knock by Dimuth. He has played a big role in stretching this lead to 253 runs.
Short in length and around off, Mathews stands back and pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Lands it on a good length around off, shaping back in, Mathews covers the line and defends it solidly.
Lunges and defends it towards short leg.
Karunaratne has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Dropped! Too quick for Markram at short leg. Sharp spin back into the batsman from around off, Karunaratne tries to defend but it takes the inside edge and quickly flies towards Markram. He sticks his left hand out but it brushes it and goes to backward square leg.
Continues from over the wicket for the left-hander as well. A flighted full ball on off, Dimuth defends it off his front foot.
Turns it off his pads through square leg for a run.
Loopy full ball on middle, defended back off the front foot.
On a length around middle and off, it's worked through backward square leg for a single.
Mistimed! Rabada goes full this time and bowls it wide outside off, Mathews plays a loose drive on the up and it goes a bit uppishly towards mid off.
Shortish and on off, defended from the crease to the off side.
Slightly short and outside off, angling in a bit, Mathews defends it back from the crease.
Mathews has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Good length ball on off, defended off the back foot.
Kagiso Rabada returns into the attack.
Arm ball on middle, landing on a fuller length. Mathews gets forward to defend but it takes the inside edge and runs to fine leg for a single. Lead - 250!
Loopy on middle, it has been worked with the spin through mid-wicket for a single.
Walks down the track and forces it right back. This time Maharaj makes the stop with a dive to his right.

FOUR! Bang! Karunaratne shimmies down the track to a full ball and hammers it past the left side of the extra cover for a boundary. No stopping this one. He has batted particularly well against Maharaj.
Action replay of the previous delivery.
Flighted ball landing wide outside off, a bit of inward turn, Karunaratne pads it away.
Gets on the front foot and blocks to end the over.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Goes on the back foot and punches it to short cover.

Wrong 'un, turning back into the batsman, Karunaratne picks it from the pitch and hence is late in keeping it out. Beaten in air but not off the deck. The ball in the meantime rolls in the gap at cover-point and they cross.
Tossed up on off, defended off the front foot.
FOUR! Brilliant shot! Shamsi bowls a flighted full ball on off, spinning away after landing, Karunaratne drives it through extra cover for a boundary.
Flighted and outside off, left alone.
Mathews has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Floated and full on off, Mathews is a bit squared up as he defends it from the outer half of his blade.

15th Test fifty for Karunaratne, last time I wrote this, he went on to score a century. Another one incoming? He nudges this delivery to covers and crosses for a run. Continues to bat with authority. By the look of things, it appears that he is batting on a totally different pitch. Doing his best to make his 50th Test a memorable one. A century in first innings and now a half century. Only the second Sri Lankan to do so.
Flighted on middle, defended on the leg side.

Appeal for an lbw! A sharp spin from outside off, Karunaratne gets across a bit as he tries to defend it off his back foot. Misses the ball to get hit on the pads. They appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Probably struck him in line but it's turning too much and could have missed the leg stump.
Loopy and on middle, defended to short leg.
Throws this one up and outside off, Mathews tries to drive through covers but it spins back in to take the inside half of the bat. He ends up mistiming back to the bowler.
Too full in length around off, Mathews flicks it across the line and Bavuma at short mid-wicket makes a diving stop.
Driven through mid off by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Floated and full on off, Karunaratne goes down on one knee and lap sweeps it down to fine leg for a couple.
Short and wide outside off, Karunaratne mistimes his square cut.
Flatter ball on off, defended off the back foot.
Short outside off, cut straight to point.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Not out! Never left the crease. A delivery sliding down the leg side, Mathews strides forward and then tries to work it away off his pads. He misses and then de Kock takes the bails off. For a second, it appeared that Mathews lost his balance and his back leg might have come out. They appeal, it's referred upstairs but the replays find nothing much to please the tourists.
Stumping appeal! That's a quick glovework by Quinton de Kock. Has Mathews' back leg left the crease momentarily?
Quicker one, darts in on middle, turning away a bit, Mathews immediately shifts his weight on the back foot and defends it out.
Flighted and on off, defended off the front foot back to the bowler.
Nicely tossed up ball on off, landing on a fuller length and spinning away, Karunaratne gets forward and pushes it with gentle hands to point.
Full toss on middle, whipped across the line but Maharaj did well at mid-wicket to stop the racing ball.
Tossed up and on off, defended off the front foot.

Flighted and on off, turning back in, Mathews tries to play it with a straight bat but it takes the inner half of the bat and rolls towards backward square leg. The fielder there makes a diving stop but cannot prevent the single.
Loopy and on middle, Mathews defends it off his front foot to the leg side.
Floated and on leg, worked with the spin to mid-wicket.
Spinning back in from around off, helped to square leg.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
FOUR! A flighted ball on off, Karunaratne is down the track immediately and drills it back past the bowler for a boundary. He continues on his merry way, completely unfazed.
FOUR! Very well played! Tossed up ball landing outside off, Karunaratne gets across the stumps and plays a well-executed paddle sweep through short fine leg for a boundary.
Tries to drive it through the line but ends up mistiming it back to the bowler.
Flighted and landing outside off, Karunaratne jumps out of the crease and then tries to defend. But it spins back in to take the inside edge. Luckily for Dimuth, it goes wide of short leg.
Flighted and outside off, a bit on the shorter side, Mathews watchfully defends it from the back foot.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Spin and bounce after landing around middle, Mathews stays back to work it around but misses to take a blow on his body.
The batsman dances down the track but decides to defend it.
Defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Short and outside off, Karunaratne gets back and slaps it to sweeper cover for a run.
Tabraiz Shamsi is back on.
Flighted full ball on off, Mathews defends it off his front foot. Two wickets and a run from the over, a brilliant one by Maharaj.
Drinks break. Angelo Mathews meanwhile has joined Karunaratne in the middle with Sri Lanka leading by 225 runs.

OUT! Mendis is dead in front. Enough part of the ball landed on the leg stump line. Keshav can continue to celebrate. This is the 5th duck bagged by Kusal in Tests, second at this venue. Coming to the delivery, once again Maharaj gives it good air and gets it to spin away. Mendis also is caught napping on the back foot as he misses the ball to get hit on the back pad. They appeal and the finger goes up. Mendis has a clueless look on his face, looks at his partner and then takes the DRS. We thought the ball pitched outside leg but that's not the case in the replays and the Ball Tracker shows three reds. A good phase of play for the Proteas but they are way behind in this Test.
Kusal Mendis is adjudged lbw! He looks at his partner and then takes the referral. Only pitching seems to be an issue as otherwise everything looks adjacent. Let's see...
Arm ball on off, defended off the front foot.
Spin and bounce, outside off, left alone by Mendis.
Kusal Mendis is the new batsman.

OUT! Sound of timber! That's a dream delivery. Maharaj is delighted. He produces a gem to dismiss Dhananjaya. Gives this one a good toss in the air and lands it around leg. It spins away from there to square up the batsman in defense and then goes on to kiss the top of off stump. What a sight for any bowler. Maharaj is doing his bit to keep South Africa somewhere in this Test match. De Silva got stuck inside the crease, could have done better with his front foot movement.
Takes a step down the track and flicks it past the diving mid-wicket fielder. Steyn there dived over the ball and let it pass. A single taken.
Full and on off, blocked from the crease to end the over.

Back of a length delivery on off, Dimuth punches it off his back foot towards extra cover. The fielder there reacts to his left but fails to stop. Although du Plessis manages to do so with a dive after coming from mid off. A single taken.
Identical to the last delivery, once again it has been worked across the line but straight towards the mid-wicket fielder.
Good length ball on middle and leg, helped off the pads but straight to mid-wicket.
Lands it on a length close to the off stump line, Karunaratne defends it off his back foot.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
SIX! This shot has 'enough is enough' written all over it. Gives the charge to a tossed up delivery around off, reaches the pitch of the ball in a flash and powers it over long on for a biggie.
Gets on the front foot to a full ball and presents a straight bat in defense.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Ufff...that's a very risky stroke. Maharaj slips in an arm ball outside off and it skids back in after landing. Dhananjaya gets back inside the crease and then plays a very late cut, almost off the off stump. Manages to place it behind point, Bavuma chases it down and they take a couple.

Advances down the track to a fuller length ball and pushes it right back. The bowler dives to stop it to his right but ends up kicking it wide of mid on. There is a run on offer but they decide not to cross.
Flighted full ball on off, defended off the front foot to the off side.

Oohh...that stayed low. Philander serves it on a good length around off, holding its line and keeping low. Dimuth sticks back to put bat on ball but it beats the inside edge and goes on one bounce to the keeper.
Once again Philander is on the pads of the batsman. Karunaratne tickles it through square leg for a run.
Full and on middle, easily worked behind square leg for a single.
Length delivery slanting down the leg side, Dhananjaya tries to flick but misses.
Good length ball on off, it's defended off the back foot to the leg side.
Angles in a full length ball on off, de Silva works it off his pads to mid-wicket.
A slip and gully in place for the new batsman as Philander runs in to bowl.
Flighted full ball on off, defended of the front foot to the off side.
Dhananjaya de Silva is the number 3 batsman.

OUT! Gunathilaka holes out! This is absolutely against the run of play. Keshav tosses this one up in the air and lands it on a fuller length outside off. It curls back in after pitching as Danushka skips down the track for a big shot. He probably wanted to go straight but on the point of impact his bat turns in his hands and he ends up ballooning it towards wide long on. Rabada in the deep runs across to his left and takes the catch safely. Maharaj is all pumped up in his celebration. Sri Lanka lead by 212 runs.
Strides forward and plays it with soft hands to point for one.
Tossed up ball landing outside off, Dimuth gets well across the stumps in an attempt to play the reverse sweep but misses. It goes very closely past the off pole.
Gets forward to a full ball and defends it with the spin to mid-wicket.
Slower delivery landing outside off and spinning in, Karunaratne walks down the track and then tries to defend. Not sure he middled that.
A length ball on off, Dimuth stays back to push it towards Rabada at point who misfields and parries it behind. They pick up a single. End of a harmless over. The 50-run stand is up. Lead is 211.
Karunaratne has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
FOUR! That's a poor delivery. An overpitched on outside off, Karunaratne offers the full face of the bat and drills it down through mid off for a boundary.

With a silly mid off in place, Philander runs in and delivers a length ball outside off. Gunathilaka pushes it with an angled bat towards backward point where Rabada dives to his right to make a partial stop. Danushka waits for it and then decides to cross. A bit of misunderstanding but they eventually complete the run with ease.
Fuller and on off, Gunathilaka gets forward and defends it near his front pad.
Push and a miss! Full and outside off, going away from the batsman with the angle, Gunathilaka has a tame poke inside the line but misses.
Vernon Philander gets a first look-in in this innings.
The batsman plays a sweep shot. They pick up a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Tossed up delivery outside off, left alone.

Aerial, catch, catch, the bowler screams but... Flighted full ball landing outside off and turning back in, Dimuth tries to play the reverse sweep but it takes his gloves (probably) and loops on the off side. The keeper runs across to his left, Amla from first slip also reacts (just for the sake of reacting) but the ball lands safely.
Walks down to the pitch of the delivery and forces it down to long on for a run.
Big spin and bounce into the batsman from outside off, Karunaratne stays back to defend but it takes the inside edge and hits him on the pads.
In the channel outside off, leaving the batsman after landing, Gunathilaka makes a leave.
Slip comes up. Only a gully in place now. There is a third man present as well.
Good length ball outside off, pushed past the point fielder for a run. All too easy at the moment for the Sri Lankan openers.
Effort ball. Steyn bends his back as he lets out a back of a length ball around off, Gunathilaka sticks inside the crease and at the very last moment runs it down to third man for a single.
Bouncer again, on off, it's been ducked under by the batsman.
Bowls it full and outside off, Danushka plants his front foot forward, watches the line closely and then decides not to offer any shot.
Steyn steams in and bangs in a bouncer around middle, Gunathilaka ducks underneath it.
The batsman dances down the track and does well to block the ball.
Another sweep shot by Gunathilaka but this time it goes straight to the fielder in the deep at square leg and they take only a run.

Quicker and fuller on off, Danushka goes down and across to sweep it past Maharaj at backward square leg. He dives but fails to make the stop. Dean Elgar cuts it off in the deep and they take a couple of runs. Lead crosses 200 now!

Runs down the track and seeing that the bowler bowls it wide outside off. Gunathilaka somehow reaches there and then tries to defend. It takes the inside half of the bat and goes a bit uppishly but wide of short leg.
Flatter this time, outside off, Danushka gets across the stumps and defends.
Floated full ball landing outside off, it has been defended off the front foot by Gunathilaka.
Lands it on a length around off, angling away again, Karunaratne plays from the crease to the off side.
Karunaratne opens the face of the bat and helps it to third man. Two runs added to the total.
Fullish and outside off, driven square of the wicket on the off side but straight to the point fielder.
In line of the stumps, tapped towards mid-wicket for a single.
Angling away from the batsman, on a fuller length, Gunathilaka is lured into the cover drive but fails to make any connection.
Short in length and on middle, it has been eased down to fine leg via a pull shot for a single.
Jumps out of the crease this time to smother the spin and then defends it back to end the over.
Allows the ball to spin back into him and then dead bats it on the leg side.
Turning into the batsman from the rough outside off, DG tries to sweep but misses to get hit on the pads. The impact was outside off and hence no real appeal.
Loopy ball on off, turning in again with extra bounce, Danushka helps it quietly to backward square leg again.
Flatter and shorter outside off, defended from the back foot to the off side.
Tossed up delivery on off, spinning in, Gunathilaka moves back and helps it off his pads to backward square leg.
Another delivery drifting down the leg side, Gunathilaka fails to flick and it goes off his pads to fine leg. A leg bye taken. Going on easily, Sri Lanka.
Once again the line of the delivery is quite straight and it has been worked away in front of square leg for a single.
An inswinger by Steyn but the line is middle and leg. Dimuth fails to flick and is hit on the pads. A stifled appeal for an lbw dies down quickly.
FOUR! Eased away! Width on offer outside off, Karunaratne camps back inside the crease and just guides it through backward point for a boundary.
On a length around middle and off, defended off the back foot.
Starts with angling a full ball away from the batsman, Dimuth pushes it with an angled bat through the gap at cover-point for a couple.
We're back for the last session. A minimum of 27 overs left in the day's play. The players are back on the field and it will be Dale Steyn to steam in first up. All set, here we go...
...DAY 2, THIRD SESSION...

Faf du Plessis will be disappointed with the score. He should have had at least a wicket by now but has seen the new ball almost being seen off. None of his bowlers has bowled badly but he needs that wicket column to be filled in quickly. The lead has swelled to 186 and Faf will hope that he tries and gets the Lankans all out within the next 100 runs. Join us back at 1500 local (0930 GMT) for the remaining 27 overs of the day.

Nice period for the Lankans. They could have lost a wicket or two but have managed to survive the tricky period. Gunathilaka started off in an attacking fashion but has then slowed down, becoming cautious. Karunaratne on the other hand, has been more agile, taking all the singles on offer and rotating the strike more often.
Another back foot defense to end the over and session. TEA ON DAY 2, SRI LANKA LEAD BY 186!
Landed outside off, defended from the crease.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Tossed up outside off, Gunathilaka comes down the track to flick but is not to the pitch of the ball. Misses his flick and the ball lobs off his pads to the vacant off side.
Excellent yorker, a rarity in Test cricket. Karunaratne jams it out to the bowler.
Outside off, punched through the covers where the fielder does extremely well to make a half-stop. Two runs taken.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman has punched that ball through the off side.
Stays back and blocks.
On a length outside off, watchfully defended to the off side.
Kagiso Rabada is back on.
Around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Outside off, Danushka stays back and defends.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. One run added to the total.

DROPPED! Lazy from Bavuma. Full and outside off, Gunathilaka gets across and paddles it uppishly. Temba Bavuma does extremely well to run to his left from square leg, gets to the ball but then takes it lightly and puts it down. A single taken.
A touch short, punched past short leg for a single.
Outside off, a play and a miss.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot for a single.
On middle, flicked past short leg.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off.
Full and around off, spinning away, Gunathilaka looks to defend but the ball takes the outside edge and goes past slip.
Spin from both ends. Tabraiz Shamsi comes on to bowl. The ground staff is as ready as a swimmer, about to dive into the pool on the gun shot.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Comes down the track and pushes it to long on for a single.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.

UMPIRE'S CALL! So close... some solace for South Africa that they do not lose a review. But this wicket would have raised their morale. Not all that short, outside off, but Danushka creates his own length by going back to a ball which should have been played on the front foot. Misses his flick and is hit on the pads. He had walked across and hence perhaps the umpire thought that the impact was outside off. The Proteas ponder for a while before getting it reviewed and the impact is indeed UMPIRE'S CALL.
An early review. Maharaj thinks Gunathilaka is LBW. Where is the impact?
Comes down the track, gets to the pitch of the ball and defends it.
Full and outside off to start, watchfully defended.
Keshav Maharaj is brought on to bowl. Meanwhile, it has gone overcast and the ground staff is getting ready with the covers. It rained at around 1420 local yesterday.
Outside off, left alone.
The batsman has punched that ball through the off side.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Outside off, punched through the covers for a couple.
Bouncer! The batsman does well to evade it.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
The batsman has punched that ball through the off side.
Fuller and around off, watchfully blocked out.
Around off, watchfully defended.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
FOUR! Edged away. On a length outside off, Karunaratne pushes at this one and gets a healthy outside edge - but wide of second slip - to the third man fence.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. Two runs added to the total.
Goes back in his crease and blocks.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
On middle and leg, Karunaratne chips it uppishly through mid-wicket for a couple. Poor running. Vernon Philander was only jogging from mid on. There was an opportunity for the third.
Around off, defended towards cover.
Around off, defended from the crease.
The batsman has been struck on the thigh pad.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.

NEARLY A CHANCE! Another slower ball on middle, once again Danushka is early into his straight drive. He just pushes this back, ending up chipping it aerially. Steyn puts in a leap for the return catch but the ball eludes him.
On middle, pushed towards mid on.

Oohhh... smart ploy from the bowler. He comes running in, giving the impression that he is going to bowl at 150 clicks. Instead, he bowls a slower ball, completely deceiving Gunathilaka. The southpaw is months early into a forward push and ends up chipping it uppishly. Luckily or him, there is no mid off and he gets a couple.
Dale Steyn to bowl from the other end.
The batsman has driven that ball straight back. One run added to the total.
Outside off, left alone.
The batsman has punched that ball through the off side.
Outside off, a play and a miss.
Pitched outside leg, Danushka misses his flick and is hit on the pads.
FOUR! Flashy stroke to get going. On a length, not all that short, outside off, Gunathilaka throws his bat at it and gets it behind point for a boundary.
